title: The Flooded Bell Chapel
story: Deep in the drowned sea-chapel, Vossmire the Tide Gullet gulps in the ocean and spits it back out, making the water climb higher and higher. On a narrow stone ledge above the flood, a litter of six otter pups huddles and squeaks. Mr 6 jams his shield into the drain-hole and cranks the old bilge pump, but the pump alone cannot win — he needs to know exactly how much time he has.
question: Vossmire pushes the water up 6.25 inches every minute, while Mr 6's pump drains 3.75 inches every minute, and the pups' ledge sits 30 inches above the water right now — how many minutes does Mr 6 have before the water reaches the ledge?
solution: Each minute the water really rises 6.25 - 3.75 = 2.5 inches.
Mr 6 has 12 minutes to carry the pups up the bell rope.
praise: Dividing into the 30-inch gap was exactly the right move — the missing step was subtracting the pump's 3.75 inches to find the REAL rise each minute.
hint: The water goes up and the pump pulls it down at the same time. What is the net change in the water level in one single minute?
victory: Mr 6 ferried all six pups up the bell rope with ninety seconds to spare, and Vossmire — with nothing left to flood — sulked out to sea making rude bubble noises. The otters now ring the chapel bell at high tide, just to show off.
imagePrompt: A brave numeral-six knight with a blue cape cranking an iron bilge pump in a half-flooded sea chapel while a wide-mouthed eel-like tide monster spouts green water, six otter pups shivering on a mossy stone ledge above, cold blue light through broken windows.
